plain_english.headline: A broad market, with volatility around normal. Best fit: goldilocks — yields falling without credit breaking.
because: The average stock is keeping up with the index — the rally is broad.
Single stocks are moving about as much as the index. The index itself is quiet, with VIX at 15.2, lower than 86% of the past two years.
Option dealers are positioned in a way that damps moves — rallies get sold into and dips get bought.
Trend-following funds are mixed across the 18 markets we track, and none is at an extreme — the positioning is not crowded.
Big speculators are unusually long the dollar, the S&P, gold and 5 others; unusually short natural gas, the Nasdaq, silver and 1 others (CFTC data to 2026-08-18).

2 warning signs lit: breadth is rolling over toward its own average and the crowd is already positioned this way. A further 13 showed up on individual markets. No single one of these is a reason to sell. They matter when several point the same way as the breadth reading.
plain_english.so_what: Own the average stock, not just the leaders — and collect premium against it. Size at 1.00x your normal risk.
watch_for: If the dollar trades above 99.45 (0.3% away), trend funds start buying.
If the 2-year trades above 103.72 (0.8% away), trend funds start buying.
Watch for single stocks becoming more volatile while the index stays calm. That gap is the earliest warning we get.
This reading would strengthen if IWM flat (roc5 -0.92%, roc20 3.59%) reversed.

levels.if_it_breaks: Below here stocks move together and selection stops paying. Only direction matters in that regime.
Above this, protection is already expensive. A spike through it is not a fresh reason to sell.
Low correlation means stocks trade on their own news and selection pays. Rising back through the middle of its range means everything starts moving together again, and only direction matters.
